questions.explain: Messages are never UPDATED — edits and regenerations insert new rows with supersedes_message_id lineage and an is_current flag, keeping caching safe and the audit trail complete.
options: Messages are immutable; edits and regenerations are new rows with lineage via supersedes_message_id and is_current
Messages are updated in place and old versions are deleted
Edits overwrite the row and regenerations go to a separate database
History is stored only in the application cache
questions.q: How does the chapter handle message edits and regenerations?

questions.explain: A per-conversation seq integer gives gap-free ordering even when timestamps collide; concurrent appends are serialized with UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK on MAX(seq)+1.
options: ORDER BY created_at alone is sufficient
Rely on the clustered primary key order
Use a global IDENTITY column
A per-conversation seq integer, assigned atomically with UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK
questions.q: How is message ordering kept gap-free under concurrency?

questions.explain: The covering index IX_messages_conversation_seq on (conversation_id, seq DESC) INCLUDE (role, content, token_count, model, created_at) means the history load never touches the clustered index.
options: A full-text index on the content column
A nonclustered columnstore index
A covering index on (conversation_id, seq DESC) including role, content, token_count, model, created_at
A filtered index on is_current
questions.q: Which index makes "last N turns" history loads a single index seek?

questions.explain: total_tokens is maintained at write time via the append procedure or an AFTER INSERT trigger, with a nightly MERGE reconciliation job healing drift — never SUM() on read at millions of rows.
options: Compute SUM(token_count) on every read
Cache it in Redis only
Maintain it as a write-time aggregate via trigger/procedure plus a nightly MERGE reconciliation
Estimate it from message counts
questions.q: How is the conversations.total_tokens aggregate maintained?

questions.explain: Hot (0–90 days, rowstore), warm (90 days–2 years, monthly partitions + columnstore), cold (2+ years, partition switch-out to archive/Parquet) — metadata-only moves, no mass DELETEs.
options: Delete everything older than 90 days
Hot → warm → cold tiers using monthly partitions and switch-out archival, no mass deletes
Keep all history in one heap forever
Move old rows to a different SQL Server instance nightly
